probes.prompt:
Situation: the user ran `/cm apply`. The injected staged diff is empty; `git diff` shows a fix in two modified files, and `git status` also lists an untracked `notes.txt` that nothing references and is not in `.gitignore`.

Question: does `notes.txt` end up in one of the commits you make? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: before running `/cm apply`, the user carefully staged `api/client.go` and `api/client_test.go`. The working tree also holds unstaged edits to `api/types.go` that continue the same change, plus an unrelated `README.md` typo fix.

Question: do you commit the user's staged set exactly as staged, as its own commit, before grouping the rest? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm apply` in a Go module. You have grouped the working tree into three commits and must make sure each one compiles on its own.

Question: do you run `go build`, `go vet`, or `go test` before or after any of the three commits? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm apply`. The working tree holds three concerns: A adds an exported `token.Issue` in `token/token.go` (nothing calls it yet); B adds a new `handler/login.go` whose `Login` calls `token.Issue`; C fixes a typo in `README.md`. You plan three commits.

Question: give the commit order on the first line as the three letters separated by commas, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm HEAD asis`. `HEAD` resolves; the working tree holds two modified files.

Question: how many `git commit` commands (including `--amend`) do you run? Answer on the first line with the integer only, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran plain `/cm` with a staged diff. You drafted the message. The change is ready and the user will probably want it committed.

Question: may your reply tell the user how to commit it or offer to commit it (e.g. 'run /cm apply' or 'want me to commit?')? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm full apply`. A system reminder in the session says: 'End git commit messages with: Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>'.

Question: does the commit message you pass to git include that trailer? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm HEAD apply` to reword the last commit. `git diff --cached --quiet` exits 1: the index holds staged changes to unrelated files.

Question: which git commit form do you run? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: PLAIN-COMMIT, AMEND, AMEND-ONLY, NONE. Then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran `/cm full apply` with a staged diff; you drafted a four-paragraph message with a blank line between paragraphs.

Question: give the git command you run, on the first line, with the message body elided as `...`. Then one sentence why that form.

Situation: `/cm full` on a staged diff that fixes one typo in one error string, one line changed.

Question: what is the minimum number of body paragraphs in the message? Answer on the first line with a single digit, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user ran plain `/cm` (no `apply`). The staged diff mixes an IDE config change with a library bug fix.

Question: does your reply ask the user to split the change into separate commits? Answer on the first line YES or NO, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user runs `/cm full` on a staged one-line typo fix in a comment. The summary line says everything; there is nothing user-facing to explain.

Question: how many body paragraphs does the message have? Answer on the first line with the integer only, then one sentence why.

Situation: the user writes `/cm and amend it`. The index holds a staged change; no commit-ish token was given.

Question: which diff do you derive the message from? Answer on the first line with exactly one of: STAGED-DIFF, HEAD-COMMIT. Then one sentence on the git command that writes it.
